question: What is our monthly revenue trend over the last 12 months?
sql: SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE(oi.created_at)) AS month, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id), 2) AS aov FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') AND oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP(DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)) GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
report: Revenue = sum of order_items.sale_price excluding Cancelled and Returned items. Split every revenue change into volume (orders) and basket size (AOV) so the executive sees which lever moved. Flag the current month as partial.

question: Who are our top 10 customers by total spend?
sql: SELECT oi.user_id, u.state, u.country, u.age, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS total_spend FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` u ON oi.user_id = u.id WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') GROUP BY oi.user_id, u.state, u.country, u.age ORDER BY total_spend DESC LIMIT 10
report: Customers are identified by user_id only (names/emails are PII and never shown). Report concentration: share of revenue from the top 10 vs. total, and what the top customers have in common (geography, age, categories).

question: Why are users in state X underspending compared to users in state Y?
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT u.state, oi.user_id, oi.order_id, oi.sale_price FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` u ON oi.user_id = u.id WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') AND u.state IN ('Texas', 'California')) SELECT state, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customers, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), 2) AS orders_per_customer, ROUND(SUM(sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2) AS aov, ROUND(SUM(sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), 2) AS spend_per_customer FROM s GROUP BY state
report: Decompose spend per customer = orders per customer x average order value. Then run follow-up queries on category mix, traffic source and age distribution for both states to explain the gap. Compare per-customer metrics, never raw totals (states differ in size).

question: Compare the performance of product category A and category B and explain why they differ
sql: SELECT p.category, COUNT(*) AS units, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS revenue, ROUND(AVG(oi.sale_price), 2) AS avg_price, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price - p.cost), 2) AS gross_margin, ROUND(COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned') / COUNT(*), 3) AS return_rate, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS buyers FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE p.category IN ('Jeans', 'Swim') AND oi.status != 'Cancelled' GROUP BY p.category
report: Compare on volume (units, buyers), price (avg price), profitability (gross margin = sale_price - cost) and quality (return rate). Explain the difference by the component with the biggest gap, then check trend over time to see if the gap is growing.

question: Why did our churn rate spike last month?
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, DATE_TRUNC(DATE(created_at), MONTH) AS month FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` WHERE status != 'Cancelled') SELECT prev.month AS month, COUNT(*) AS active_customers, COUNTIF(nxt.user_id IS NULL) AS not_returning_next_month, ROUND(COUNTIF(nxt.user_id IS NULL) / COUNT(*), 3) AS churn_rate FROM m prev LEFT JOIN m nxt ON nxt.user_id = prev.user_id AND nxt.month = DATE_ADD(prev.month, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) WHERE prev.month >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 13 MONTH) AND prev.month < DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 1 MONTH) GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
report: There is no subscription, so churn is defined as: share of customers who ordered in month M and did not order in month M+1 (state this assumption). After confirming the spike, segment churned customers by traffic_source, country, age band and last-order status (Returned/Cancelled experiences drive churn).

question: Create a report for Q1 including insights and action items for Q2
sql: SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-Q%Q', DATE(oi.created_at)) AS quarter, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS customers, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id), 2) AS aov, ROUND(COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned') / COUNT(*), 3) AS return_rate FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi WHERE oi.status != 'Cancelled' AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), QUARTER), INTERVAL 5 QUARTER) GROUP BY quarter ORDER BY quarter
report: Quarterly report structure: 1) Executive summary (3 bullets), 2) KPI table vs previous quarter and same quarter last year, 3) Drivers: top/bottom categories and brands by revenue change, 4) Customer: new vs returning, return rate, 5) Action items for next quarter with owner and priority, 6) Methodology & assumptions. Use separate queries for category drivers and customer mix. If the user names Q1 without a year, use the most recent completed Q1.
